input: Repository: roboflow/rf-detr ITEM #1647 Type: issue State: open Title: FP16 export decoder drops detections retained by PyTorch sigmoid Author: user-1 Created: 2026-10-22 Labels: (none) Body: ### Search before asking - [x] I searched existing issues and PRs for sigmoid/FP16 decoder reports and did not find this specific problem. ### Bug The shared NumPy export decoder rounds each sigmoid operation in `float16`. This changes threshold and top-k decisions relative to native PyTorch sigmoid on the **same FP16 logits**, including a comparison with CUDA. For the exactly representable logit `1.1005859375` and threshold `0.75`: | Calculation | Probability | Retained by strict `score > 0.75` | | --- | ---: | --- | | Current NumPy decoder | 0.75 | No | | Native PyTorch FP16 sigmoid, CPU and tested CUDA backend | 0.75048828125 | Yes | | Mathematical sigmoid | approximately 0.7503698765343172 | Yes | Affected code: [`decode.py` at current develop `5b22dfc`](https://github.com/roboflow/rf-detr/blob/5b22dfc0940697ce1abdfa681a5f7392b3eddbfb/src/rfdetr/export/_runtime/decode.py#L106-L107). This concerns CPU NumPy post-processing. It can also consume FP16 outputs produced by GPU inference; native PyTorch CUDA sigmoid itself does not exhibit this particular intermediate-rounding problem. ### Environment - RF-DETR develop: `5b22dfc0940697ce1abdfa681a5f7392b3eddbfb` (still current develop when filing). - Linux x86-64, Intel Core i7-12700H. - CPU project validation: Python 3.12.12, NumPy 2.3.5, PyTorch 2.14.0+cpu. - Additional CPU/CUDA comparison: Python 3.10.9, NumPy 1.25.2, PyTorch 2.1.0+cu121, NVIDIA RTX 3070 Ti Laptop GPU. - No model weights, training, or GPU are needed for the minimal reproduction. ### Minimal reproducible example Run against the affected revision: ```python import numpy as np import torch from rfdetr.export._runtime.decode import decode_detections boxes = np.array([[0.5, 0.5, 0.2, 0.2]], dtype=np.float32) logits = np.array([[1.1005859375]], dtype=np.float16) decoded = decode_detections(boxes, logits, (100, 100), threshold=0.75) reference = torch.from_numpy(logits).sigmoid() print("NumPy decoder:", decoded.confidence.tolist()) print("PyTorch FP16:", reference.flatten().tolist()) print("PyTorch retained:", int((reference > 0.75).sum())) ``` Actual: ```text NumPy decoder: [] PyTorch FP16: [0.75048828125] PyTorch retained: 1 ``` ### Additional The FP16 arithmetic for this input is: ```text exp(-x) -> 0.332763671875 1 + exp(-x) -> 1.3330078125 1 / (1 + exp(-x)) -> 0.75 ``` Other concrete consequences: - `sigmoid(-12)` overflows in the current FP16 exponential and returns zero. Native PyTorch FP16 returns `6.139278411865234e-6`. The existing `[-88, 88]` clip protects an FP32 exponential, but does not protect FP16. With `np.errstate(over="raise")`, a negative class logit can raise during decoding even when another class has a high score. - Logits `8` and `9` both become `1.0` in the current decoder, while PyTorch FP16 yields `0.99951171875` and `1.0`. A `num_select=1` case can therefore select the lower-confidence query because the NumPy results tie. These are synthetic, deterministic examples; I have not measured their frequency in trained-model outputs or any mAP impact. The proposed correction is to compute the entire sigmoid with at least FP32 precision and round once back to the original score dtype **before** top-k and thresholding. This preserves strict threshold semantics and FP16 score ties. FP64 inputs should retain FP64 precision. One owned work array can be reused for the intermediate operations. Related prior art: ONNX Runtime fixed the same class of intermediate FP16 precision loss in [CUDA sigmoid PR #14727](https://github.com/microsoft/onnxruntime/pull/14727). ### Are you willing to submit a PR? - [x] Yes, I have prepared a focused fix and regression tests. AI-assisted tools helped investigate the issue, prepare the fix, and write the reproducer. The reported checks ran against the source versions described above.
